text: Confirm scope: DiscountPolicy.discountRate applies a 10% bulk discount when subtotalCents >= 10_000 for REGULAR-tier customers (VIP always gets 20% regardless of subtotal, so use CustomerTier.REGULAR / default Order constructor for these tests to isolate the bulk threshold).

In /src/test/java/com/sweforge/pricing/PricingCalculatorTest.java, add three new @Test methods matching the existing style (single Item per order via `new Order(List.of(new Item(cents)))`, assertEquals on calculateTotalCents result): just below threshold (9,999 cents) expecting no discount (total 9,999); at threshold (10,000 cents) expecting 10% discount (total 9,000); just above threshold (10,001 cents) expecting 10% discount (total 9,001).

Name the new test methods descriptively and consistently with existing naming, e.g. subtotalJustBelowBulkThresholdHasNoDiscount, subtotalAtBulkThresholdGetsBulkDiscount, subtotalJustAboveBulkThresholdGetsBulkDiscount.
Do not modify any file under /src/main/java (production code must remain unchanged) - verify by diffing only the test file after edits.
Run the targeted test class, e.g. `mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test`, under Java 21 to confirm the new boundary tests pass alongside existing ones.
Run the full test suite with `mvn test` to confirm no regressions elsewhere, per repository convention of finishing with a full-suite run.
New tests compile and pass for 9,999 (no discount), 10,000 (10% discount), and 10,001 (10% discount) subtotal cents.
`mvn -Dtest=PricingCalculatorTest test` passes with all (existing + new) tests green.
`mvn test` (full suite) passes with no failures.
No changes present in any file under /src/main/java - only PricingCalculatorTest.java is modified.
